name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Rob Menendez running with large fundraising edge
No Republican on ballot; independent challengers underfunded
model.rationale: The D+15 district, Menendez's incumbency and roughly $2 million raised against independents with no reported fundraising make this a Safe D race, and Polymarket prices a Democratic win at 95%.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or a well-funded independent surge could narrow the margin, though a Menendez loss remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Rob Menendez seeks reelection in a northern New Jersey district that leans Democratic by about fifteen points. He enters the general with roughly $2 million raised and outside support, while his opponents are independents with no visible fundraising or outside spending. No Republican candidate appears on the ballot, leaving Aristotle Eliopoulos as the main challenger.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial advantage, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 95%. The seat remains safely in Democratic hands, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
